title: T-Rex sprite: the dino and the cacti are drawn as pixel-art bitmaps inside their collision boxes — standing, running (two frames), jumping and dead — with the rules untouched
body:
## Context

The game is complete as rules (t1 jump, t2 obstacles, t3 score), but the renderer (`src/render.js`) still draws the dino and the cacti as plain rectangles with `fillRect`. This ticket gives them a look — the Chrome T-Rex, in pixel art — **without touching a single rule**: `src/game.js`, `src/rng.js` and every existing key of `src/tuning.js` stay as they are, and the headless player's output for a given seed stays byte-identical. The picture is a function of the state the rules already expose (`tick`, `distance`, `dino.onGround`, `over`, each obstacle's box) and nothing else. No image files, no dependencies (DECISIONS.md D4): the bitmaps are data in a module.

## Scope

1. `src/sprites.js` (new, browser-free — `npm run lint` applies to it): the bitmaps and one pure function.
   - A bitmap is an array of equal-length strings, `'#'` for a filled cell and `'.'` for an empty one. Provide: `DINO.stand`, `DINO.run` (an array of TWO frames that differ in the legs), `DINO.jump` (legs together), `DINO.dead` (e.g. a different eye), `CACTUS.small`, `CACTUS.tall`. Any reasonable T-Rex silhouette is fine: head to the right, tail to the left, an eye, an arm, two legs.
   - `export function spriteFor(state)` returns `{ pose, frame }`: `pose === 'dead'` when `state.over`; `'jump'` when `!state.dino.onGround`; `'stand'` when on the ground and `state.distance === 0`; otherwise `'run'` with `frame = Math.floor(state.tick / TUNING.sprite.runFrameTicks) % 2`. Pure, deterministic, no randomness.
   - `export function cactusFor(obstacle)` returns `'tall'` when `obstacle.h >= TUNING.sprite.tallCactusFrom`, else `'small'`.
2. `src/tuning.js` (additive only): `sprite: { runFrameTicks, tallCactusFrom }`.
3. `src/render.js`: draw the dino by mapping the chosen bitmap onto the dino's box — cell width `dino.w / columns`, cell height `dino.h / rows`, one `fillRect` per filled cell — and each obstacle by mapping its cactus bitmap onto the obstacle's box the same way. Ground, score, `HI` and the game-over text stay as they are.
4. Tests (`tests/sprites.test.mjs`): the criteria below, with a fake 2D context that records `fillRect` and `fillText` calls (the existing render test shows the pattern).
5. Docs, in the same commit as the change: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (sprites module, the pose function), `docs/TICKETS.md` (t4 to Done), `DECISIONS.md` (a line: the picture is a function of the state; bitmaps as data, no assets).

## Acceptance criteria

- D1. `spriteFor` on a fresh run returns `{ pose: 'stand', frame: 0 }`; after some `NO_INTENT` ticks on the ground it returns `pose: 'run'` and its `frame` alternates 0/1 every `TUNING.sprite.runFrameTicks` ticks; while `dino.onGround === false` it returns `'jump'`; when `over === true` it returns `'dead'` regardless of the rest. The same state always gives the same result.
- D2. Every rectangle `render` draws for the dino lies inside the dino's box (`x >= dino.x`, `x + w <= dino.x + dino.w`, same for y/h, within 1e-6) — the picture never exceeds the collision box, in every pose.
- D3. Every rectangle drawn for an obstacle lies inside that obstacle's box; `cactusFor` returns `'tall'` for `h >= tallCactusFrom` and `'small'` below it, and the two cactus bitmaps differ.
- D4. The two run frames differ in at least one cell; `jump` differs from both run frames; `dead` differs from `stand`.
- D5. Regression: the existing render assertions still hold — the zero-padded score and `HI` are still printed with `fillText`, and the game-over text appears only when `over`.
- D6. The rules did not change: `src/game.js` and `src/rng.js` are byte-identical to the tree before this ticket (`git diff --stat <before>..HEAD -- src/game.js src/rng.js` is empty), the only change to `src/tuning.js` is the additive `sprite` key, and `npm run play -- --ticks 600 --every 100 --seed 7` prints exactly the same output as before the change.
- D7. The gates are green on the integrated tree: `npm test && npm run lint && npm run build`.

## Out of scope

Ducking pose, birds, clouds, day/night, a sprite for the score digits, sound, any change to collision boxes or rules. Whether it "looks like a T-Rex" is a matter of taste: the criteria above are the contract, and the aesthetic judgement, if anyone wants one, goes to the founder.

## References

`docs/TICKETS.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `DECISIONS.md` (D1, D4), `src/render.js`, `src/tuning.js`, `src/game.js` (read-only), `tests/score.test.mjs` (the fake-context pattern), `scripts/play.mjs`.
